points.description: Identifies a stack as a data structure (not merely a list, array, or general storage location).
States that a stack stores elements/items.
States the last-in-first-out (LIFO) property: the last item added is the first to be removed, or equivalently uses the term LIFO / last-in-first-out.
points.partial_credit: All-or-nothing: the LIFO property must be stated clearly.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the answer to identify a stack as a data structure, say that it stores elements/items, and clearly state the last-in-first-out property. Award part marks for the definitional components present, but P3 is all-or-nothing and needs a clear LIFO statement. Vague answers such as 'items are added and removed' without the order do not earn P3.
